summary: Both occurrences reviewed. No entry addition, new sense or form box is warranted from this set; the current entry's text and numbering are retained.

69/468 is already the inherited II Preterit example. It has a feminine zero-marked experiencer, l-stimulus and an inchoative event after seeing the boy. The reflexive German gloss does not imply Turoyo Detransitive.

92/27 has a stative ʕašəq yo predicate and a d-clause specifying seeing the human form. The item lacks the mʕašaq-/mʕašəq formation of the inherited II paradigm and may be a borrowed adjective/agent noun. Its actual fondness meaning is recognized, but stem/box/sense assignment remains unresolved.
The snake participant and stative predication do not justify inventing I base forms or a new II sense by translating German liebt. No independent idiom has been established.
Is ʕašəq yo at92/27 a lexical borrowed adjective/agent noun, or a Part act. within a productive Turoyo paradigm? Supply contrasting gender, plural or finite forms.
If this predicate is admitted to the glossary, should its d-clause fondness construction be an adjective note or a separate verbal sense? Current corpus evidence cannot determine that.
